Bevor and Während: German B1 Time-Clause Practice

Choose bevor for an earlier main action and während for simultaneous actions. Practise temporal clauses with the finite verb at the end.

B1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions + writing task

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Try the exercisesWrite your own sentence

Understand the rule

Bevor means before and introduces an event later than the main-clause action: Ruf mich an, bevor du losfährst. Während can link events happening at the same time: Während ich bügle, hört er einen Podcast. Both are subordinating conjunctions and put the finite verb at the end.

Common mistake to avoid

For this lesson, während expresses time. It can also express contrast in other contexts, so read the whole sentence rather than translating it mechanically.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Notice the form that changes and the role it plays in each sentence.

Worked example 1Ruf mich an, bevor du losfährst.Call me before you set off.
Worked example 2Während ich bügle, hört er einen Podcast.While I iron, he listens to a podcast.
Worked example 3Wir prüfen die Adresse, bevor wir das Paket schicken.We check the address before sending the parcel.
Worked example 4Während die Kinder malen, bereitet Eva das Essen vor.While the children draw, Eva prepares the food.

Practice: fill in the gaps

Use bevor for before and während for simultaneous while; conjugate the verb where a verb cue is supplied. Try each question before opening the answer. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich speichere die Datei, ___ ich das Programm schließe. (before)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: bevor

Saving happens before closing the program.

Question 2. ___ sie kocht, deckt er den Tisch. (at the same time)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: Während

The two actions happen simultaneously.

Question 3. Warte hier, bevor du die Straße ___. (überqueren, present)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: überquerst

Du takes überquerst, and the finite verb closes the bevor-clause.

Question 4. Während der Drucker arbeitet, ___ ich die Unterlagen. (sortieren, present)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: sortiere

The finite verb of the main clause follows the fronted subordinate clause.

Use it in your own sentence

Describe washing your hands before cooking and listening to music while cooking.

Try writing your answer before reading the model below. Other natural answers are possible.

One possible answer

Bevor ich koche, wasche ich mir die Hände. Während ich koche, höre ich Musik.

Check your wording: Bevor orders events; während expresses overlap. Both subordinate clauses are verb-final.

What to practise next

Change the subject or noun in one model sentence. Check the verb form, case and word order before comparing it with the rule.

Try the gaps again on another day without reading the explanation first. If a choice is still unclear, use the linked grammar foundation before moving to another topic.
